Airbnb: Seasonal Fluctuations in Its Quarterly Revenue

Airbnb Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) primarily generates its revenue by operating a global digital marketplace that directly connects independent hosts offering a wide variety of accommodations and unique local experiences with guests seeking temporary lodging options across the globe.

It recently introduced new artificial intelligence tools designed for dynamic property pricing while updating its global house rules policy and launching an exclusive travel booking partnership directly with American Express.

Chewy: Gradual Upward Trends in Quarterly Revenue

Chewy Inc. (NYSE:CHWY) primarily earns its revenue by functioning as an online retail enterprise that provides essential pet food, prescribed medications, and general health and wellness supplies to domestic companion owners across the United States.

It recently updated the annual fee and rewards structure of its paid membership program and expanded its physical operational footprint by hosting an open house for a new veterinary clinic located in Colorado.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue here refers to the data provider's standardized income-statement revenue line item, and this basic financial metric matters because it shows investors the total amount of money coming into an organization from its business operations before any operating expenses are deducted.

Foolish Take

Normally, the first thing to note when examining a company's revenue trend is seasonality: some times of the year have stronger buying patterns than others. For most stocks, compare revenue year over year, by quarter. In normal times, seasonality holds true for consumer stocks like these as well. Airbnb gets exceptional volume for summer months in the Northern Hemisphere, which translates into third-quarter revenue being booked. Chewy has less seasonality, generally around the Christmas season like most retailers. The strength of its autoship program mitigates seasonality; however, one would expect its increasing focus on veterinary services to smooth out seasonality as well.

American Express reported higher third quarter 2026 net income of US$3,712 million and raised full year earnings guidance while keeping revenue growth expectations unchanged.

Fresh card partnerships with Airbnb and Albertsons expand American Express's travel and everyday spending reach, deepening its fee and rewards ecosystem across both premium and mass market customers.

The focus now turns to how American Express's stronger earnings guidance and ecosystem expansion might influence its longer term investment narrative.

See how American Express compares with other card networks and lenders by focusing on resilient balance sheets and fundamentals in our curated list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals (25 results)

American Express Investment Narrative Recap

To own American Express, you need to be comfortable with a model that leans hard into premium customers, rich rewards, and high marketing and engagement spend against a high debt load. The raised 2026 EPS guidance and strong recent earnings keep that narrative intact. The key shorter term swing factor remains whether spending volumes and fee income can keep pace with those customer engagement costs.

The biggest operational risk still sits in rewards and co brand transitions. Variable customer engagement expenses already run at about 44% to 45% of revenue and portfolio sales are expected to weigh on billed business and net interest income through late 2026. The recent quarter and guidance update do not remove that pressure but they help reduce near term concern around it.

The most relevant fresh development for this story is American Express tapping bond markets with several new callable, senior unsecured variable rate notes totalling US$3.0b that mature in 2030 and 2034. This matters because the group already carries a high level of debt and relies entirely on higher risk wholesale funding rather than lower cost customer deposits.

For you as an investor, these offerings shape how the company funds ongoing card growth, marketing, and technology spend, and how interest expense trends against net interest income. Execution now is about keeping returns high while managing refinancing and rate risk on that wholesale funding stack. Any slip there would quickly feed back into the margin and earnings narrative investors are focused on.

What The Current Analyst Scenario Implies For American Express

American Express' narrative projects US$98.3b revenue and US$15.4b earnings by 2029. This rests on analysts assuming 11.5% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of about US$4.1b from US$11.3b today.

title: Airbnb owners hit by £800m tax raid
detail:
Airbnb owners hit by £800m tax raid
Jonathan Prynn
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 6:54 AM MST 3 min read
ABNB
Trade Airbnb on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
An estimated 450,000 Airbnb properties in Britain are available for short-term lets - iStock

Hundreds of thousands of Airbnb owners will be hit by John Healey's Budget tax raid on landlords, piling yet more pressure on Britain's tourism industry.

Treasury sources confirmed that short-term holiday lets will be hit by the 4pc additional tax on property income, as well as landlords renting out houses and flats for tenants to live in.

The surprise raid on the rental sector was one of a series of Budget tax grabs announced by the Chancellor on Wednesday, which will be used to fund headline giveaways such as the £100 energy bills handout to households.

Basic-rate income taxpayers will see the tax rate on property income rise from 20pc to 24pc from next April. Those in higher tax bands will see the rates on rental income rise to 44pc and 49pc.

Rachel Reeves had already signalled a 2p increase in her Budget last November, but Mr Healey went further in his Commons statement on Wednesday.

Industry leaders said the extra tax would be another significant blow for a sector still reeling from the prospect of a "holiday tax" on overnight stays from 2028.

Alistair Handyside, of the Professional Association of Self-Caterers, said: "It is incredibly unhelpful at a time when tourism is under so much pressure; it's yet another payment to find.

"A lot of people are going to say, 'I've done the maths, it's just not worth it any more.' It's not any individual straw that breaks people; it's the cumulative impact.

"All the costs are going up and now the Government is taking more, and of course we're not able to put up prices, so everyone's margin decreases again. They can't keep doing that; it just doesn't work."

OBR estimates suggest the new higher rates of property income tax will raise around £1bn in the 2028‐29 tax year before settling at around £800m in later years.

Pavan Mandir, at advisers UK Landlord Tax, said an Airbnb owner in the higher-rate tax band making a typical £24,000 profit will see their tax bill rise by £960 from £9,600 to £10,560.

An estimated 450,000 Airbnb properties in Britain are available for short-term lets.

Alongside rival online platforms such as Airbnb, Booking.com and Expedia-owned Vrbo hosted more than 100 million stays last year.

Many are owned by businesses or do not yet earn enough to pay income tax, leaving around 130,000 individuals declaring a total of £2.5bn in profits from holiday lets last year, according to HMRC.

Short-term holiday lets had not been classified as property businesses until April last year when a more generous tax treatment under the furnished holiday lettings regime was abolished.

Mr Mandir said: "Since the furnished holiday lettings regime was abolished from April 6 2025, holiday lets and Airbnb-style lets have formed part of your ordinary property business.

"That means there is no separate treatment for short-term lets."

Airbnb declined to comment.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Airbnb (ABNB) stock fell 4.6% in the week to October 27, 2026, while the S&P 500 edged up 0.14%. The shares now trade 11.4% below their highest close of the past year. For anyone holding the stock, the bigger worry is what a market-wide sell-off would do. When the whole market has fallen before, how far did Airbnb stock drop, and how long did it take to come back?

How Far Airbnb Stock Fell In Past Market Shocks

Since its shares began trading in December 2020, Airbnb has weathered five market shocks. The stock recorded its largest fall during the 2022 inflation shock, as the Fed tightened. In that period, the shares dropped 48%, while the S&P 500 lost 24%. Across all five shocks, Airbnb fell 28.0% on average, against a 13.4% decline for the index.

Recovery times varied widely. The shares needed a median of 6.3 months to climb from a low back to their earlier high. Two of those waits ran past a year. Airbnb took 16.0 months to recover from the 2025 US tariff shock. After the 2022 shock, the wait stretched to 49.7 months, and the stock only got back to that high in August 2026.

How Does Airbnb's Business Compare With A Year Ago?

Airbnb is growing faster than it was a year ago. Revenue rose 16.5% in the quarter ended June 30, 2026, outpacing the 12.7% growth posted in the same quarter of 2025. Over the past twelve months, sales reached $13.2 billion, up 13.6% from the twelve months before.

The company's operating margin improved in that quarter, but the measure remains lower over the full twelve months. The margin reached 21.0% in the June quarter, up from 19.8% a year earlier. Over the past twelve months it was 20.8%, against 22.5% in the preceding twelve-month window. Airbnb also holds far more cash than debt, reporting $12.1 billion in cash and short-term investments at the end of June 2026 against $2.5 billion of debt.

What Risks Is Airbnb Facing Now?

Airbnb faces the prospect of tighter rules in Europe, pressure on its prices, and a profit margin that management expects to slip slightly in the September quarter. News reports on September 9, 2026, indicated that new EU plans would give European cities more leeway to curb short-term rentals such as Airbnb. On an August 6, 2026, call, management called policy a risk, but not an existential one, that the company will manage forever.

At the time of that call, about half of Airbnb's active listings were on a single service fee. Management expects all of its listings to adopt the fee by the end of 2026, and said this fee puts downward pressure on pricing, an effect management wants so that Airbnb offers guests more value and stays priced competitively against other platforms. For the full year, management expects its implied take rate, the share of bookings Airbnb keeps as revenue, to be relatively flat against 2025. That outlook accounts for higher customer incentives tied to new businesses.
